DBS consistently demonstrates the lowest discontinuation rates, while pump-based therapies, particularly subcutaneous infusions, show higher early dropout rates related to adverse events, device complications, neuropsychiatric symptoms, skin reactions, or insufficient efficacy. Intestinal levodopa therapies generally show intermediate persistence rates, although device-related complications remain common. Emerging evidence suggests that education, clinical experience, and structured patient support may reduce discontinuation from newer subcutaneous levodopa as well as apomorphine therapies. Patients who discontinue one DAT remain eligible for another. Shared decision-making and multidisciplinary evaluation remain essential to optimize long-term outcomes and treatment persistence in advanced PD. Future prospective comparative studies are needed to standardize DAT selection, clarify optimal switching strategies, and improve long-term treatment retention rates in patients.

title: Marker-based CRISPR screens identify POU2F1 as a regulator of DLL3 and neuroendocrine identity in small cell lung cancer.
authors: Cunniff PJ, Fitzpatrick C, Bauer J et al.
abstract: Small cell lung cancers (SCLCs) often exhibit a neuroendocrine lineage identity marked by high expression of Delta-like ligand 3 (DLL3). Because DLL3 shows minimal expression in normal adult tissues, it serves as an SCLC-selective tumor antigen and is the basis for clinically efficacious targeted therapies. Understanding the mechanisms that regulate DLL3 expression is therefore critical for advancing therapeutic strategies in this disease. Here, we performed transcription factor-focused and genome-wide CRISPR screens to identify regulators of DLL3 expression in SCLC. Both approaches converged on POU2F1 as a top activator of DLL3 in this tumor context. Despite its ubiquitous expression, we identify an SCLC-specific role for POU2F1 in activating DLL3 and a broader set of neuroendocrine lineage genes. Epigenomic analyses reveal tandem POU2F1-ASCL1 motifs within the DLL3 promoter that underlie the functional cooperativity between POU2F1 and the neuroendocrine master regulator ASCL1 for high-level DLL3 expression in SCLC. We provide evidence that tandem POU2F1-ASCL1 elements are part of a cis-regulatory code for the lung neuroendocrine cell fate. Together, these findings define a previously unrecognized transcriptional logic controlling DLL3 expression and establish POU2F1 as a context-specific regulator of neuroendocrine lineage in SCLC.

title: High-flow nasal cannula-based support for suspected severe immune-related pneumonitis in a patient with small cell lung cancer: a case report.
authors: Luo F, Zhu W, Hu H et al.
abstract: Severe immune-related pneumonitis (IRP) is difficult to diagnose in patients with lung cancer and competing causes of respiratory failure. We report a 69-year-old man with recurrent small cell lung cancer who developed acute hypoxemic and hypercapnic respiratory failure after multiple immunotherapies and thoracic radiotherapy. Severe IRP was suspected, although infection, tumor-related airway obstruction, mucus retention, radiation injury, and cardiac involvement remained alternative or concurrent explanations. After invasive ventilation was declined, high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) support was provided alongside corticosteroids, antimicrobials, tocilizumab, and intravenous immunoglobulin. Nursing care emphasized respiratory assessment, secretion clearance, humidification, and recognition of deterioration. Respiratory status initially improved, permitting HFNC withdrawal and discharge without supplemental oxygen. Subsequent respiratory deterioration occurred, and the patient died 178 days after admission from an unknown cause. This case highlights diagnostic uncertainty and the importance of multidisciplinary reassessment during HFNC support; concurrent treatments preclude attribution of improvement to any single intervention.

title: A Neural-Related Transcriptional Signature Is Associated with Reduced Immune Activity and Pathological Response to Neoadjuvant Chemo-Immunotherapy in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
authors: Wang Y, Liu Q, Hu L et al.

title: [Stratified Predictive Value of Dynamic Trajectories of Peripheral Blood Systemic Immune-inflammation Index for Efficacy and Survival Prognosis in Patients with NSCLC Receiving Neoadjuvant Immunotherapy Combined with Chemotherapy].
authors: Duo H, Yang Y, Yang Y et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy has become the standard treatment strategy for resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, treatment responses are highly heterogeneous, and conventional Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) radiological evaluation has limitations in predicting pathological complete response (pCR). Peripheral blood inflammatory indices can reflect the systemic immune-inflammation status conveniently and non-invasively, but the predictive value of their dynamic changes during treatment for the efficacy and prognosis of neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of dynamic changes in peripheral blood systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) before and after treatment for pCR and event-free survival (EFS) in NSCLC patients receiving neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy.
METHODS: A total of 365 NSCLC patients who received neoadjuvant therapy containing immune checkpoint inhibitors and subsequent radical resection at the Army Medical Center of PLA from January 2019 to June 2025 were retrospectively enrolled. Baseline and preoperative routine blood test data were collected to calculate SII and its decline rate. The receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was used to assess the predictive efficacy of each index for pCR. K-means trajectory analysis was performed to identify subtypes of dynamic SII changes. Multivariate Logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to analyze the associations between dynamic SII changes and pCR/EFS, with adjustment for clinicopathological variables and RECIST radiological response. To exclude multicollinearity, variance inflation factor (VIF) diagnosis was performed and highly correlated variables were removed from the multivariate Cox model.
RESULTS: The overall pCR rate was 47.95% (175/365). The area under the curve (AUC) of SII decline rate for predicting pCR was 0.701 (95%CI: 0.647-0.755). Multivariate Logistic regression showed that SII decline rate was an independent predictor of pCR [odds ratio (OR)=1.024, 95%CI: 1.017-1.032, P<0.001], which remained robust after adjusting for RECIST (OR=1.024, 95%CI: 1.016-1.031, P<0.001). K-means trajectory analysis classified patients into steady decline (72.6%), post-treatment elevation (13.7%), and high-baseline sharp decline (13.7%) groups. Compared with the steady decline group, the post-treatment elevation group had a significantly lower pCR rate (adjusted OR=0.101, 95%CI: 0.038-0.269, P<0.001; OR=0.104, 95%CI: 0.039-0.279, P<0.001 after further adjustment for RECIST). Multivariate Cox regression confirmed that SII decline rate was an independent protective factor for EFS [hazard ratio (HR)=0.682, 95%CI: 0.579-0.803, P<0.001; HR=0.692, 95%CI: 0.586-0.818, P<0.001 after RECIST adjustment]. The post-treatment elevation trajectory was an independent negative prognostic marker for EFS (HR=2.511, 95%CI: 1.555-4.056, P<0.001 after RECIST adjustment). The high-baseline sharp decline group showed a protective trend but did not reach statistical significance (HR=0.532, P=0.061).
CONCLUSIONS: Dynamic trajectories and decline rates of SII before and after treatment serve as independent predictors of pCR and EFS in NSCLC patients receiving neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy, with predictive value independent of RECIST radiological evaluation. Post-treatment elevation of SII effectively identifies high-risk patients with pathological response failure and long-term recurrence/metastasis, and can serve as a simple, non-invasive biomarker for clinical decision-making. However, these findings require further validation in large-scale prospective studies.

title: Diagnostic and Therapeutic Challenges of Mycobacterium avium Complex Pulmonary Disease in Patients with Lung Cancer: A Retrospective Case Series.
authors: Gao R, Zhu M
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the clinical characteristics, diagnostic challenges, and therapeutic management of Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary disease (MAC-PD) in patients with lung cancer, and to highlight the diagnostic limitations and treatment dilemmas encountered in this vulnerable population.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed four patients with lung cancer complicated by MAC-PD at a tertiary respiratory center in Beijing, China, between 2017 and 2025. Clinical data, cancer characteristics, underlying structural lung disease, anticancer treatments, radiological findings, microbiological results, anti-MAC regimens, and clinical outcomes were analyzed. Diagnostic methods included sputum culture, bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) next-generation sequencing (NGS), and T-SPOT.TB. The 2020 ATS/ERS/ESCMID/IDSA diagnostic framework for NTM-PD was referenced for case evaluation.
RESULTS: All four patients were male, aged 66-73 years (mean 70.5 years), with underlying bronchiectasis or structural lung abnormalities. Two had lung adenocarcinoma and two had squamous cell carcinoma. MAC-PD was detected during early anticancer therapy (n=1), during combined chemotherapy and immunotherapy (n=1), or after lung cancer surgery (n=2). Chest CT showed centrilobular nodules, tree-in-bud opacities, bronchiectasis, cavitary lesions, destroyed lung, and bronchopleural fistula, overlapping with tumor progression or bacterial pneumonia. MAC was identified by BALF NGS in three patients and sputum culture in one. In Cases 1, 2, and 4, clinical diagnoses of suspected MAC-PD were supported by BALF NGS without confirmatory mycobacterial culture. Causative organisms included M. intracellulare (n=2) and Mycobacterium avium complex not further speciated (n=2). All patients received multidrug anti-MAC therapy. Regimens were modified in two patients due to adverse events or drug-drug interactions. Two patients with destroyed lung and bronchopleural fistula had poor outcomes despite prolonged therapy (30 months and 17 months, respectively). No patient underwent antimicrobial susceptibility testing.
CONCLUSION: MAC-PD should be considered in lung cancer patients with bronchiectasis or structural lung disease when new centrilobular nodules, tree-in-bud opacities, cavitary lesions, or progressive lung destruction cannot be explained by tumor progression. Early bronchoscopy with both culture and NGS is essential; NGS should be regarded as an adjunct to, not a substitute for, culture-based diagnosis and susceptibility testing. Drug-drug interactions-particularly rifamycin-antifungal combinations-require proactive evaluation, and the combination of rifapentine with voriconazole should be avoided. Once destroyed lung develops, treatment options are limited and prognosis is poor, underscoring the importance of early detection.

title: Association between fine particulate air pollution and the risk of death from kidney cancer in Taiwan.
authors: Tsai SS, Chen CC, Chang JC et al.
abstract: The International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) has classified fine particulate matter (PM2.5) in outdoor air pollution as carcinogenic to humans. However, few studies have investigated the association between long-term residential exposure to ambient PM2.5 and kidney cancer (KC) and the available evidence remains inconclusive. Previous epidemiological studies conducted in Taiwan have reported statistically significant positive association between long-term PM2.5 exposure and several non-lung cancers. Against this background, the present study aimed to investigate the association between long-term exposure to ambient PM2.5 and mortality attributed to KC across 66 municipalities in Taiwan. Annual average PM2.5 concentrations were examined in relation to age-standardized KC mortality rates among men and women during 2010-2023. Municipalities were categorized into tertiles according to their long-term PM2.5 concentrations. Adjusted risk ratio (RRs) were estimated using multivariable regression models controlling for municipal-level lung cancer mortality (as a proxy for cigarette smoking prevalence), level of urbanization, annual household income, and physician density. A significant inverse association between long-term PM2.5 exposure and mortality attributed to KC was observed among men, whereas no marked evidence of an association was found among women. The reasons underlying this unexpected inverse association remains unclear, and the possibility of a chance finding cannot be excluded. Further epidemiological investigations are warranted to confirm these findings and clarify the potential role of PM2.5 exposure in KC development, particularly studies incorporating detailed information on PM2.5 chemical composition, source-specific exposures, and the biological mechanisms potentially linking ambient air pollution to kidney carcinogenesis.

title: [Research Progress of Active Surveillance Strategies, Psychological Distress and Behavioral Decision-making in Patients with Pulmonary Subsolid Nodules].
authors: Sun W, Zhou Y, Feng S et al.
abstract: With the widespread use of low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) in lung cancer screening, pulmonary subsolid nodules (SSNs) are being detected with increasing frequency. Persistent SSNs have malignant potential, but their natural history varies, with most lesions growing slowly and some remaining stable for prolonged periods. For SSNs with a low risk of progression, early surgical intervention may lead to overtreatment. Therefore, avoiding overtreatment while identifying the lesions with progression risk in a timely manner and determining the appropriate timing of intervention has become an important challenge in the clinical management of SSNs. Based on their imaging characteristics and natural history, active surveillance has gradually become an important management strategy for low-risk SSNs. Active surveillance appears clinically feasible in appropriately selected patients who can adhere to regular follow-up. However, during long-term surveillance, perceived illness uncertainty, risk perception, anxiety, and patient-clinician communication may influence patients' adherence to follow-up and treatment decisions. Patient education, risk communication and psychological support may help alleviate psychological distress and improve patients' understanding of their condition, although direct evidence supporting these interventions in patients undergoing long-term active surveillance for SSNs remains limited. This review summarizes the clinical evidence and implementation strategies for active surveillance of SSNs, and research on patients' psychological changes and behavioral decision-making during surveillance, with the aim of providing insights into individualized long-term management of SSNs. .

title: [Research Advances in Exhaled Breath Condensate Multi-omics for the Diagnosis and Clinical Translation of Non-small Cell Lung Cancer].
authors: Hu Q, Liu P, Zhu R et al.
abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the predominant histological subtype of lung cancer and it is characterized by high incidence, insidious onset, and poor prognosis. Early diagnosis remains challenging, as low-dose spiral computed tomography (LDCT) screening has a high false-positive rate, highlighting the need for more specific adjunctive diagnostic approaches. As a lung-proximal, non-invasive liquid biopsy, exhaled breath condensate (EBC) can directly reflect alterations in the local airway microenvironment and is increasingly emerging as an important complement to conventional liquid biopsy approaches. In recent years, EBC research has evolved from single-omics biomarker screening toward integrated multi-omics analyses encompassing genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics. Meanwhile, the introduction of technologies such as microfluidics, nanosensing, and artificial intelligence algorithms has helped overcome key challenges associated with the high dilution of EBC samples and the trace abundance of target molecules. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in EBC research, including the standardization of sample collection, multi-omics biomarker discovery, innovations in detection technologies, and clinical translation. Particular emphasis is placed on the clinical value of EBC in the early screening, molecular subtyping, therapeutic response monitoring, and early warning of drug resistance in NSCLC. Current challenges and future directions are also discussed, with the aim of providing a reference for advancing EBC-based multi-omics technologies toward precision diagnosis and treatment in clinical practice. .

title: Cardiovascular effects of chemoradiotherapy in patients with lung cancer: an [18F]FDG PET-CT imaging study.
authors: Khaing PH, Williams MC, Newby DE et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular and pro-atherogenic side-effects of chemoradiotherapy for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain a major concern given the growing burden of cancer therapy-related cardiovascular disease. Atherosclerotic plaque burden can be measured using calcium scoring while plaque activity can be assessed using [18F]fluorodeoxyglucose ([18F]FDG) positron emission tomography (PET).
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the impact of chemoradiotherapy on aortic atherosclerotic burden and disease activity in patients with advanced NSCLC undergoing repeated [18F]FDG PET and computed tomography (CT) scans.
METHODS: All [18F]FDG PET-CT scans of patients with stage 3B NSCLC from the American College of Radiology Imaging Network (ACRIN 6668) trial were retrieved from the Cancer Imaging Archive. Volumes of interest for the aorta, left ventricle and major non-cardiac organs were manually delineated. Calcium scores, mean standard uptake values (SUVmean) and target-to-background ratios (TBRmean) were quantified, and comparisons before and after treatment scans performed.
RESULTS: Twenty-six patients (mean 60 ± 9 years, body-mass index 25 ± 5 kg/m2) met the inclusion criteria, with 23 having aortic atherosclerosis as evidenced by the presence of aortic calcification. Pre- and post-treatment scans were performed approximately 14 weeks apart. After chemoradiotherapy, aortic calcium score increased by 10% in calcified plaques (p < 0.05) and aortic [18F]FDG TBRmean uptake increased by 4% (p = 0.02). There were no changes in [18F]FDG uptake in other organs.
CONCLUSION: Chemoradiotherapy has adverse effects on the vasculature, possibly through increased inflammation resulting in accelerated atherosclerotic disease. This increased cardiovascular risk in lung cancer survivors highlight the need for aggressive risk factor modification at the earliest opportunity.

title: Predictors of radiation-induced lymphopenia in NSCLC: blood and bone marrow dose during chemoradiotherapy.
authors: Nowicka Z, Beekman C, Mohan R et al.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Radiation-induced lymphopenia (RIL) is a significant complication for patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) undergoing radiotherapy, particularly as immunotherapy becomes increasingly integral to treatment. Understanding the predictors and mechanisms underlying RIL will support and help direct efforts to preserve anti-tumor immunity and optimizing therapeutic outcomes.
METHODS: This study assessed the relationship between radiation dose to the blood and bone marrow and the development and recovery of lymphopenia in two (training and validation) cohorts, 134 patients in total, with NSCLC treated with either proton (PSPT) or photon-based chemoradiotherapy (CRT) between June 2009 and March 2014. Compartmental blood flow models and automatic organ segmentation were used to quantify radiation doses to circulating blood, large vessels and proliferating bone marrow. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify significant predictors of severe lymphopenia within 2 months from CRT start and its recovery.
RESULTS: We found that both the generalized equivalent uniform dose (gEUD) to blood and baseline absolute lymphocyte count (ALC) were significant predictors of grade 4 lymphopenia. The discriminative ability (measured by AUC) for blood dose gEUD peaked around negative alpha values, suggesting that low-dose contributions to the blood pool are most relevant for predicting lymphopenia risk. Despite proton therapy delivering mean blood doses lower by 12.1% (p = 0.006) compared to photon therapy, there were no significant differences in nadir lymphocyte counts between the modalities. Bone marrow dose was only weakly correlated with lymphocyte nadir and showed no association with lymphocyte recovery after treatment.
CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that radiation dose to circulating blood is a significant predictor of radiation-induced lymphopenia in NSCLC patients. Despite the observed correlations, these findings suggest that optimizing radiation dose to the blood alone may not be the most effective strategy for reducing lymphopenia.

title: Prognostic Impact of Checkpoint Inhibitor Pneumonitis: Results from a Multicenter Prospective Observational Study (CS-Lung004).
authors: Yamaguchi K, Yano J, Kanaji N et al.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) is a potentially life-threatening adverse event caused by anti-programmed death-1 (PD-1) and programmed death ligand-1 (PD-L1) antibodies. However, paradoxical findings have been reported regarding the association between overall survival (OS) and CIP. This study aimed to prospectively evaluate the relationship between the 2-year OS and CIP in patients receiving first-line treatment, including anti-PD-1/PD-L1 antibody therapy, using 3-month and 1-year landmark analyses.
METHODS: A multicenter prospective observational study was conducted between December 2021 and November 2023 to evaluate the prognostic impact of CIP, based on timing and severity, in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
RESULTS: Although no significant difference in OS was observed between patients with and without CIP developed within 2 years or 1 year, the 3-month landmark analysis showed that patients who developed CIP within 3 months had significantly shorter OS than those who did not (median OS from the 3-months landmark: 11.1 months with CIP versus not reached without CIP; log-rank p = 0.011). In multivariate Cox regression analyses, using patients without CIP as the reference group, CIP within 3 months was significantly associated with impaired overall survival (any-grade CIP: hazard ratio [HR] = 2.22, 95% confidence interval [CI]=1.21-4.09; Grade 3-5 CIP: HR=3.37, 95% CI=1.57-7.23).
CONCLUSION: This was the first prospective study to demonstrate the prognostic value of CIP. CIP within 3 months after the initiation of first-line treatment, including anti-PD-1/PD-L1 antibody, especially Grade 3-5 CIP, was associated with shorter OS in patients with NSCLC.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Lung Diseases: Screening, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prognosis.
authors: Chen F, Yang J, Zhang Y et al.
abstract: Pulmonary diseases currently pose significant threats to global health, spanning common chronic conditions including lung cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and asthma, as well as infectious and inflammatory diseases like tuberculosis, interstitial lung disease (ILD), and COVID-19. Therefore, accurate diagnosis, effective therapeutic strategies, and reliable assessment of prognosis for pulmonary diseases are essential for improving patient outcomes and safeguarding public health. Despite the increasing availability of medical imaging and pathological data owing to improvements in detection technologies, what is becoming increasingly evident are the limitations of conventional diagnosis, which relies solely on clinicians' subjective judgment based on imaging, pulmonary function, pathology, and clinical experience. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) technology, especially machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), has made significant progress in areas such as image recognition and model construction. Numerous studies have demonstrated the widespread application of AI in the screening and diagnosis of lung diseases, the optimization of treatment strategies, and prognosis assessment, revealing its remarkable ability to process and interpret complex clinical data. Although concerns persist regarding data quality, the "black box" nature of algorithms, clinical practice, and the regulatory landscape, the application of AI in lung disease research and clinical care is more and more promising. In this review, we summarize the latest advances of AI in the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary diseases, analyze the challenges and limitations of current AI technologies ranging from data and algorithms to clinical translation, and highlight directions for future research.

title: High-grade intrasalivary thymic-like carcinoma: comprehensive histopathological and molecular characterization and a critical appraisal.
authors: Oon ML, Schubart C, Hölsken A et al.
abstract: Neoplasms exhibiting thymic differentiation are rare tumors that may occur at non-thymic locations including the thyroid and major salivary glands. Wh​ile recent work has reframed salivary gland tumors with thymic differentiation as occurring along a morphological continuum ranging from benign to overtly malignant cases, the high-grade end of this spectrum remains poorly characterized. We present three cases of high-grade intrasalivary thymic-like carcinoma (ISTC), subjected to detailed histomorphological, immunohistochemical and molecular characterization. These tumors arose in the parotid (n = 2) and submandibular gland (n = 1), and showed common morphological features of lobular growth, intervening fibrous bands, syncytial growth of spindled-to-epithelioid cells and dense intratumoral and peritumoral lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, reminiscent of a lymphoepithelial carcinoma. Immunophenotypically, the tumors showed consistent expression of CD5, CD117 and BCL2 and squamous markers. All cases were EBV-negative. Next-generation sequencing showed heterogenous, non-recurrent mutations and absence of gene fusions. The clinical course was variable, with one case showing prolonged survival despite metastases, and another showing rapid dissemination and death. High-grade ISTC appears to be a morphologically defined but molecularly heterogeneous entity, and recognition of the morphological and immunophenotypical gestalt is essential for accurate characterization.

title: Successful Treatment of Pembrolizumab-associated Myositis-myocarditis-myasthenia Gravis Overlap Syndrome with Gastrointestinal Pseudo-obstruction Using Zilucoplan: A Case Report.
authors: Komatsu H, Yamada M, Wako K et al.
abstract: Myositis-myocarditis-myasthenia gravis (MMM) overlap syndrome is a rare, potentially fatal complication of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. We report a 74-year-old man with pre-existing thymoma and anti-acetylcholine receptor antibody positivity who developed pembrolizumab-induced MMM complicated by gastrointestinal pseudo-obstruction (GIPO). Despite the administration of corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulin, ocular symptoms persisted, and bowel dysmotility progressed. We initiated zilucoplan, a complement C5 inhibitor. Within days, diplopia and dysphagia resolved, and GIPO markedly improved on radiography, enabling oral intake. To our knowledge, this is the first case of pembrolizumab-induced MMM treated with zilucoplan and the first ICI-mediated GIPO managed with a complement inhibitor.

title: Zybrivo (sintilimab): CHMP positive opinion
